title: Ordinary scalar and geometric comparison respects scalar composition
statement: Let X be a scheme and A, B, C arbitrary commutative rings in the independent coefficient universe. Let f:A -> B, g:B -> C and h:A -> C with e:h=g composed with f. Use the insertion-normalized ordinary scalar extensions and geometric inverse images of [lem-sfb-adic-finite-reduction-data]. For a specified composite sheaf ring map, transport adicFiniteChangeComp along the equality of ring maps; write alpha and beta for this transported scalar reassociation on the etale and pro-etale sites respectively. Write theta_f, theta_g, theta_h for adicFiniteOrdinaryComparison and p_A,p_C for ordinary geometric inverse image. For every etale A-module M, beta_(p_A M) followed by theta_h(M) equals change(g_pro)(theta_f(M)), followed by theta_g(change(f_et) M), followed by p_C(alpha_M). No derived category, flatness, nonzero-ring or finiteness assumption is involved.

source.place: Lemmas lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict and lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; the ordinary tensor-insertion calculation in step 2 of lem-sfb-adic-comparison-composition.

proof.text: Transport the ordinary scalar balancing isomorphism along h=f followed by g. Its normalization is insertion(f), followed by insertion(g), followed by balancing = insertion(h); this follows by equality induction from adicFiniteChangeComp_insertion. Naturality of scalar insertion follows from the normalized ordinary scalar adjunction unit. Naturality of pullInsertion follows by composing the inverse-image underlying comparison with scalar insertion.

Construct a candidate comparison for h by first applying inverse pro-etale balancing, then scalar extension of theta_f, then theta_g, then geometric inverse image of etale balancing. To check its normalization, rewrite the composite etale insertion as the two successive insertions and balancing. Naturality of pullInsertion moves etale balancing to the far right. Apply normalization of theta_g and then of theta_f. Naturality of scalar insertion moves theta_f through the second insertion. Finally the two pro-etale insertions equal composite insertion followed by inverse balancing. This is exactly the required normalization for the candidate.

Uniqueness in adicFiniteOrdinaryComparison_existsUnique identifies the constructed candidate with theta_h. Precompose its component equality with pro-etale balancing and cancel balancing with its inverse. The resulting equality is the assertion. These equations hold also for zero modules, zero rings and identity coefficient maps.

theorem adicOrdinaryComparison_composition (X : Scheme.{u})
    {A B C : Type (max v (u + 1))} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    (f : A →+* B) (g : B →+* C) (h : A →+* C) (e : h = g.comp f)
    (M : Mod (constant (smallModelComparisonEtaleTopology.{u, v} X) A)) :
    (adicOrdinaryChangeComp
        (adicFiniteConstantMap f (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X))
        (adicFiniteConstantMap g (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X))
        (adicFiniteConstantMap h (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X))
        (adicFiniteConstantComp _ f g h e)).hom.app
          ((adicFiniteOrdinaryPullback.{u, v} X A).obj M) ≫
        (adicFiniteOrdinaryComparison.{u, v} X h).hom.app M =
      (change (adicFiniteConstantMap g (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X))).map
          ((adicFiniteOrdinaryComparison.{u, v} X f).hom.app M) ≫
        (adicFiniteOrdinaryComparison.{u, v} X g).hom.app
          ((change (adicFiniteConstantMap f
            (smallModelComparisonEtaleTopology.{u, v} X))).obj M) ≫
        (adicFiniteOrdinaryPullback.{u, v} X C).map
          ((adicOrdinaryChangeComp
            (adicFiniteConstantMap f (smallModelComparisonEtaleTopology.{u, v} X))
            (adicFiniteConstantMap g (smallModelComparisonEtaleTopology.{u, v} X))
            (adicFiniteConstantMap h (smallModelComparisonEtaleTopology.{u, v} X))
            (adicFiniteConstantComp _ f g h e)).hom.app M)
